title: Chapter 10: Landforms Created by Running Water (Fluvial Geomorphology)

blocks.content: Running water is the most powerful agent of erosion and deposition on the Earth's surface. Rivers shape valleys, transport sediments, and create extensive depositional plains. Fluvial geomorphology studies the processes and landforms associated with rivers.
Running water is the most powerful agent of erosion and deposition on the Earth's surface.

items: Questions often test the primary agent of Earth's surface erosion—remember that running water is the most powerful agent.
Be prepared to define Fluvial Geomorphology as the study of river-related processes and landforms.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Running water serves as the most powerful agent of both erosion and deposition on Earth.
River systems shape valleys, transport geological sediments, and build extensive depositional plains.
Fluvial geomorphology focuses specifically on understanding the processes and landforms associated with rivers.
